solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fierce drunk in Brazilian port

indicators.note: a drunk word staggers about, so the letters of fierce are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild, inebriated reveller loose in a South American harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges FIERCE into the port's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Recife is a major Atlantic seaport city in north-eastern Brazil.

clue.text: Rose phoned again?

definitions.meaning: rose as in rose up, revolted
whimsically, ..., rang on the bell once more

explanation.surface: A flower and a repeat call make an odd pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower or a name but is the verb 'rose up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise in revolt; the joke splits it as re-bell, ring again.

clue.text: Sounds like German chap suffered, being diminished

indicators.note: the clue says the name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Kurt is a German man's name
ailed means was ill or suffered

explanation.surface: A German man was unwell and wasted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' applies only to the name Kurt, which is said the same as the word for brusque.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailed means cut short or reduced, so being diminished in extent.

clue.text: An oldie into rock?

parts.note: suggests an ageing music fan, but means something ancient turned into stone

explanation.surface: An elderly person who loves rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into rock' reads as a fan of the music; really it is something old literally turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved remains of an ancient organism set in stone; also slang for an old person.

clue.text: Gossip about a daughter away from home — one looking for pleasure?

indicators.note: gossip placed about the next pieces means it wraps round them

parts.note: to gab is to chatter or gossip
someone away from home is out

explanation.surface: A tattling relative chatters about a daughter who has left home to enjoy herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the gossip word round 'a daughter'; 'away from home' looks like part of the definition but supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a pleasure-seeker who flits from one social outing to another.

clue.text: Practice in the country when deal is wanted?

definitions.text: Practice in the country when deal is wanted?

parts.words: Practice in the country when deal is wanted?
parts.note: deal is timber, so this is growing trees in the countryside

explanation.surface: A rural trade custom when someone needs a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' suggests a business bargain, but it is softwood timber such as pine.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboriculture is the cultivation of trees, which supply timber.

clue.text: Island worker on Lammas standing on head

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word standing on its head is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Lammas Day falls on 1 August, written Aug I

explanation.surface: A labourer on harvest festival day doing a headstand.
explanation.walkthrough: Lammas, an old English harvest festival, is 1 August: AUG I; 'standing on head' reverses it to IGUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: One appears in gown erotically — one having a certain something

indicators.note: the answer appears within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone shows up in a seductive gown and has a certain allure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in 'gOWN ERotically'.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner possesses something, whatever that particular item may be.

clue.text: The fellow is entertained by abstemious sort of believer

indicators.note: being entertained, as a guest is, means going inside the host word

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means abstemious
he is the pronoun for the fellow

explanation.surface: A man is hosted by a sober, religious type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts HEIS inside TT, the abbreviation for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God or gods, a particular kind of believer.

clue.text: Man responsible for stink, reverse of gentleman

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink

indicators.note: the reverse of the word for a gentleman is that word read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone to blame for a bad smell, the very opposite of a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns the gentleman's title back to front; 'responsible for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris is a male first name, so it serves as an example of a man.

clue.text: Character in position behind reversing vehicle

indicators.note: the position word comes behind the reversed vehicle
a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so its word is read back to front

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor stands in place behind a vehicle that is backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the vehicle round, and 'behind' sets the position word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance, like character, means solid worth or moral weight in a person.

clue.text: Register theft when this aggressive person has run wild

indicators.note: letters that run wild scatter, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thug's rampage ends with theft from a cash register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has run wild' rearranges REGISTERTHEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A street fighter is a combative brawler who fights in public places.

clue.text: Having more green growth in meadow before terrible fire

indicators.note: the meadow word comes before the rest

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters of fire are jumbled

explanation.surface: A field with lusher foliage until a dreadful blaze sweeps through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the fire into IER, which 'before' places after the meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafier is the comparative of leafy, describing plants with more foliage.

clue.text: Looks at final expression of goodwill

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means looks at or considers
A closing greeting at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone glances over a farewell message wishing the reader well.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to gaze at; 'kind regards' is a standard sign-off in correspondence.

clue.text: Fish caught by reel sometimes

indicators.note: the answer is caught within the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: An angler's reel occasionally lands a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' points to the letters running across 'reEL Sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snake-like fish found in rivers and seas.

clue.text: Liking singing in church, having joined the fold?

indicators.note: the singing word has joined the fold word, following on

parts.note: a pen is a fold or enclosure for sheep
a chant is a liturgical song sung in church

explanation.surface: A newcomer who enjoys hymns has become a member of the congregation, the 'fold'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fold' plays on a church flock, but here it is a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or fondness for something.

clue.text: Attempt to restrict a piper playing somewhere in Ireland

indicators.note: the attempt word restricts, holding in, the other letters

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: playing about means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying to stop a bagpiper performing somewhere on the Emerald Isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' gives IPPERA from 'a piper', and 'to restrict' holds it inside the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a county and town in Ireland.

clue.text: Maybe young boy and knight beset by terrible dragons

indicators.note: the knight is beset by, surrounded by, the other letters
terrible dragons are in disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A child and a knight surrounded by fearsome monsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DRAGONS and 'beset by' puts N inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson can be a young boy, a child's child, though not necessarily young.

clue.text: Ruin brought by county female wanting everything

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
all means everything

explanation.surface: A greedy local woman who wants it all brings about her own undoing.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a ruin or collapse from a position of power or prosperity.

clue.text: Left with little energy after game, back in dressing-room after this?

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the game word

parts.note: whist is a card game
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Players exhausted after a match return to the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: The final whistle sends players back to the dressing-room; WHIST is a card game, not the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The referee's final whistle ends a match, after which players head off the pitch.

clue.text: Hits back in fight

indicators.note: hits sent back means the word for hits is read in reverse

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or hits

explanation.surface: Someone strikes in return during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight, especially in practice.

clue.text: Cries with bowl being empty — food to follow

indicators.note: the food word follows the empty bowl
an empty bowl has its middle removed, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: Someone wails at an empty bowl, wanting food to come next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being empty' leaves BL from BOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleats are the cries of sheep or goats, or feeble complaints.

clue.text: "Catty" type in old church group

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lot is a group or set

explanation.surface: A spiteful gossip in a parish congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catty' suggests spiteful, but means cat-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild cat of the Americas, literally a cat type.

clue.text: Drinking gin, getting sozzled alongside Scandinavian

indicators.note: the jumbled gin sits alongside, after the Scandinavian

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in northern Scandinavia

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters of gin reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A Nordic drinker knocks back gin and gets plastered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting sozzled' mixes the gin to ING, set 'alongside' the Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapping is how a cat or dog drinks, taking up liquid with the tongue.

clue.text: The king and I squeezing into small carriage

indicators.note: the letter is squeezing into the carriage word, going inside it

parts.note: a pram is a small carriage for a baby

explanation.surface: A monarch and the speaker cramming into a baby buggy.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAM is the British word for a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend.

clue.text: Dirty member of the family, fellow hiding head

parts.note: an uncle is a member of the family

indicators.note: the fellow with his head hidden loses his first letter

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A grubby relative and a man concealing his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding head' drops the fellow's first letter, leaving a two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean is a synonym of dirty, impure or soiled.

clue.text: Philosopher is alert to change

indicators.note: a change rearranges, so the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: A thinker is quick to notice when things shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges ISALERTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato.

clue.text: See notices — not just one or two

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: Look at the posters: there are far more than a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads means a great many, a quantity well beyond a couple.

clue.text: A supposed feature of beauty — yet my Mrs is different!

indicators.note: the words are made different by being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Beauty is said to need balance, but my wife's looks are an exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is different' rearranges YETMYMRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Balanced proportion is often claimed as a mark of attractiveness in faces.

clue.text: Remain to offer support, no going back

parts.note: a stay is a support, as in a brace or prop

indicators.note: the word no going back means it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Staying to help out, with no retreat possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns 'no' round; 'to offer' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain somewhere beyond the expected time.
